commit.message:
Render zap roots in comment context as '{amount} zap by @{sender}'

When a kind 1111 comment's root is a kind 9735 / 8333 zap event, the
"Commenting on …" row in `EventCommentContext` fell through to the
generic `getEventDisplayName` path. Zaps have no title/name/d tag,
so that path read the NIP-31 `alt` tag verbatim and rendered rows
like "Commenting on Bitcoin zap: 127,897 sats" — sender-less and
verbose, while the comment author obviously needs to know whose zap
they're replying to.

Add a `ZapCommentContext` branch that renders "Commenting on $100 zap
by @Alex Gleason" (or "127,897 sats zap" in sats mode, etc). The
amount link routes to the zap event itself, the @sender link routes
to the sender's profile. Both kinds are handled by the same component;
`getZapAmountSats` and `getZapSenderPubkey` from `@/lib/zapHelpers`
already encapsulate the kind-aware extraction (`amount` tag is sats
for 8333 vs. millisats / bolt11 for 9735; sender is `event.pubkey`
for 8333 vs. P tag / description.pubkey for 9735).

commit.message:
Make NoteCard's standalone zap branch kind-aware (fixes 'Anonymous zapped')

NoteCard's standalone zap layout (kind 9735 / 8333 with no `zappedBy`
overlay and no `profileZapRecipient` — i.e. a zap event rendered
directly, such as the root of a kind 1111 comment displayed as an
ancestor in PostDetailPage) had two kind-9735-only helpers baked in
that silently broke for kind 8333:

  * `extractZapSender` only checks the `P` tag / description JSON, both
    NIP-57 Lightning conventions. Kind 8333 zaps are self-signed by the
    sender, so the sender lives in `event.pubkey` and `extractZapSender`
    returns `''`. The empty string flows into `useAuthor(undefined)` and
    `getDisplayName(undefined, '')`, and the display name finally
    resolves through `genUserName('')` which returns the literal
    'Anonymous'. So a kind 8333 zap by Alex Gleason renders as
    "Anonymous zapped …" in the standalone branch, while clicking
    through to the zap event itself hits PostDetailPage's separate
    `isOnchainZap` branch (which uses `event.pubkey` directly) and
    correctly shows "Alex Gleason zapped …".

  * `extractZapAmount(event) / 1000` assumes the `amount` tag is in
    millisats (Lightning convention). Kind 8333 puts sats directly in
    the `amount` tag, so the same divide-by-1000 displays one-thousandth
    of the actual value.

Use the kind-aware `getZapSenderPubkey` and `getZapAmountSats` helpers
from `@/lib/zapHelpers` — both already handle 8333 and 9735 correctly
and are what `feedUtils.buildFeedItems` uses for the overlay path. The
existing `extractZap*` imports in this file are now unused and dropped.

Other surfaces that render zap events are unaffected: `PostDetailPage`
has separate `isZap` (9735) and `isOnchainZap` (8333) branches that
each pull the right field directly, `EmbeddedNote` routes 9735 and
8333 to distinct components (`EmbeddedZapCard` / `EmbeddedOnchainZapCard`),
and `ZapContent` already gates on `event.kind === 8333` before reading
the `amount` tag as sats.

commit.message:
Give profile-zap notifications a recipient card body

When a profile-targeted zap (kind 9735 / 8333 with a `p` tag but no
`e` tag) lands as a notification, the existing solo `ZapNotification`
renders the thin "X zapped you Y sats" header followed by an empty
`ReferencedNoteCard` (returns null because there's no `e` tag). The
result is just a single line of text with no body.

Render a `ZapRecipientCard` instead — the recipient's avatar, display
name, NIP-05 badge, and timestamp laid out the same way a NoteCard
shows its author header. Mirrors the feed rendering of profile zaps
(NoteCard.tsx's `profileZapRecipient` branch) so the same activity
has the same visual shape across surfaces. The recipient pubkey is
read from the `p` tag, which the notification query already filters
to the current user, so the body shows the receiver's own profile.

Grouped profile zaps don't need this fix: the grouping key for zaps
incorporates the referenced event id, and profile zaps have no `e`
tag, so each falls into its own group keyed by event id and never
reaches `ZapNotificationGroup`.

commit.message:
Fall back to profile-zap card when a zap's target note is unreachable

Zaps in the feed go through `buildFeedItems`, which tries to render them
as a "X zapped this note" overlay on top of the e-tagged target. When
the target note isn't in the same relay page, the wrapper is queued for
a single batched fetch; if that fetch fails, times out, or the relay
simply doesn't have the note, the zap was silently dropped from the
feed entirely. Users would see a zap they authored on their profile
page (where the page is dense with their own events and the batched
fetch is more likely to succeed) but not in their home feed — or vice
versa, depending on relay timing.

Carry the `p`-tag recipient pubkey along with each queued zap wrapper.
After the batched fetch returns, any zap whose target wasn't resolved
falls back to a standalone profile-zap card so the activity still
surfaces. This applies to both kind 8333 on-chain and kind 9735
Lightning zaps — the previous kind-9735 exclusion in the no-target
branch was on the rationale that profile-targeted Lightning zaps are
rare, but as a fallback for missing targets it would silently swallow
ordinary note-targeted Lightning zaps too. The render branch already
resolves the sender via the P-tag / description for kind 9735, so the
card displays the correct actor for both kinds.

Drop the no-target branch's kind 9735 guard accordingly. Stabilize
`feedItemKey` so a zap rendered as an overlay on one page and as a
profile-zap fallback on another collides during cross-page dedup —
both variants now key on the zap event id alone, so the same zap
never appears twice when relay coverage shifts between pages.

Regression-of: c57d99cf

commit.message:
Render profile-targeted zaps as standalone feed cards

Kind 9735 and 8333 zap events with a `p` tag but no `e`/`a` tag tip a
person rather than a specific note. Previously `buildFeedItems` required
a target event id and silently dropped these, so on-chain profile zaps
published by the wallet's Send dialog never appeared in the feed.

Surface them as a `profileZapRecipient` FeedItem variant routed through
NoteCard. NoteCard renders profile zaps with the same shape an e-tagged
zap uses — an `EventActionHeader` ("X zapped — Y sats") above the
recipient's author header (avatar + display name + nip05 + timestamp),
where the would-be target note's author block normally goes. No body
content (the zap targets the person, not a post), but the standard
action bar (reply / repost / react / zap-back / more) renders below,
wired to the recipient's kind-0 profile event so each action operates
on the identity event the zap actually targeted. Card click navigates
to the recipient's profile; the "zapped" verb in the top header links
to the zap event.

Kind 9735 profile zaps fall back to an ActivityCard because the receipt
is signed by the LNURL server (not the sender), so NoteCard's author
flow would render the wrong person. Profile-targeted Lightning zaps are
vanishingly rare in practice.

commit.message:
Point Bitcoin send success 'View transaction' at the in-app tx page

Switches the ZapSuccessScreen and the wallet Send dialog's raw-address
success view from `openUrl('https://mempool.space/tx/<txid>')` to a
React Router `<Link to='/i/bitcoin:tx:<txid>'>`, matching the existing
wallet transaction-list rows on /wallet (WalletPage.tsx:203) and the
NIP-73 link in BitcoinContentHeader.tsx:455.

The in-app NIP-73 page (ExternalContentPage → BitcoinTxHeader) is
strictly richer than mempool.space: it shows the on-chain details
*and* the kind 8333 onchain-zap attestation, the sender's Nostr
identity, and any kind 1111 comments — none of which mempool surfaces.
The link still calls `onClose` on click so the dialog dismisses
before the navigation happens.

commit.message:
Redesign wallet Send dialog to mirror the onchain zap UI

Replaces the three-step (form → confirm → success) BTC-denominated send
wizard with the single-screen USD-first flow from OnchainZapContent: big
editable USD amount, preset chips, two-tap arm for large sends, and a
fee-speed popover under the send button.

Adds a profile-autocomplete recipient picker on top of useSearchProfiles,
plus pasted npub/nprofile/nip05/hex identifiers that resolve to a pubkey.
Raw bitcoin addresses (bc1…) are still accepted as a fallback row in the
dropdown. Event identifiers (note/nevent/naddr) and the search bar's
non-profile suggestions (Wikipedia, Internet Archive, country, sidebar
nav, 'comment on URL') are intentionally excluded — every selection here
needs to be something that can actually be paid.

When the recipient is a Nostr identity, publishes a kind 8333 profile
zap after broadcast: `p` tag for the recipient, `i` tag for the txid,
`amount` tag, NIP-31 `alt`, and no `e`/`a` (profile-level zap per
NIP.md). Raw-address sends skip the kind 8333 entirely — there's no
pubkey to attribute to. Success uses ZapSuccessScreen for Nostr
recipients and a stripped-down variant (no avatar) for raw addresses.
